transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’m here because things with my wife have been… off. She says it’s just work, late meetings and little changes in her messages, and I know offices do that—my department changes meeting times all the time, actually, drives everyone mad—but with her it’s been lining up too precisely for about a year now.

It feels like there’s a private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly. I’ve tried to ignore it, but once you notice the pattern, it’s hard to just unsee it.
Have you had the feeling that your wife is sending you hidden messages or trying to communicate something secretive through these changes in her behavior?

Yes… I mean, I know how that sounds. She says it’s just normal work stuff—late meetings, different wording in messages, times shifting around. And I know offices are like that; I’ve worked in enough departments to know calendars are practically a living organism.

But with her, for about the past year, it’s been… too exact. Like the timing and the little changes line up in a way that doesn’t feel accidental. It feels like there’s something underneath it, a kind of private signal meant for me, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t actually say out loud.

Do you feel like these changes in your wife’s behavior are part of a larger pattern that only you can understand, or do you think you might be placing too much meaning on things that are actually random or normal?

I’ve wondered that, honestly. I’m not trying to make something out of nothing. I deal with schedules and emails all the time at work, and half of them are messy or random—students changing appointments, faculty sending things at odd hours, all of that.

But with my wife, it’s different. The late meetings, the slight changes in how she writes things, when she sends them… over the past year they’ve lined up too neatly. It feels like a pattern, like there’s a message in it meant for me, something she’s trying to say without actually saying it. I know other people might call it normal office stuff, but to me it doesn’t feel random.
Do you feel that other people, like friends or family, would understand or agree with the way you’re interpreting these changes in your wife’s behavior?

I don’t think most people would see it the way I do, no. My brother would probably say, “Come on, late meetings happen,” and he’s not wrong—when I was in my department, we had meetings moved three times in one week once, and everyone just pretended that was normal.

But with my wife, it’s been going on for about a year, and it’s the way the late meetings and the small changes in her messages line up. It feels too precise to be accidental. Like there’s something in it meant for me, a private signal, almost like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it straight out. I know other people might not agree, but I can’t just dismiss it.
Do you believe the messages or signals you’re seeing in your wife’s behavior have a specific hidden meaning that only you are supposed to understand?

Yes… I think so. Not like a code with numbers or anything, not like that. It’s more the timing, the way her meetings suddenly run late, and then the little changes in how she words her messages. I know she says it’s just office stuff, and I know office stuff can be ridiculous—I mean, at work I’ve seen one simple email turn into six replies about room bookings.

But with her, over the past year, it’s been too consistent. It feels like there’s something underneath it, something meant for me to notice. Like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly. I don’t know if anyone else would catch it, but I feel like I’m supposed to.
Do you feel that these messages from your wife are part of a larger hidden system or plan that you're meant to understand, or is it something more personal between the two of you?

I don’t think it’s some big system, no—not like the whole world is arranged around it or anything. It feels more… between me and her.

I mean, I’ve worked in offices long enough to know meetings run late and people change how they write emails. Sometimes our department calendar looked like someone spilled coffee on it and then tried to reorganize it. So I’m not saying every late meeting means something.

But with my wife, for about the past year, the late meetings and the little shifts in her messages have lined up too neatly. It feels private, like a signal meant for me to pick up on, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t just say out loud. I know she says it’s normal work stuff, but it doesn’t feel accidental to me.
Do you feel that the messages or signals you’re seeing from your wife might be harmful or part of something more serious, like an affair or a plot against you?

Harmful… I don’t know if I’d put it that way exactly. I mean, I’ve thought about whether it could be something serious, because why else would someone keep having these late meetings and then write just a little differently afterward? But I’m not saying there’s some plot or anything like that.

It’s more that she says it’s normal office stuff, and I know offices are like that—when I was working with faculty schedules, half the time no one knew which meeting was real until ten minutes before. But with her, over this past year, it’s lined up too neatly. The lateness, the little changes in her messages… it doesn’t feel accidental.

So I don’t know if it’s an affair or something like that. I’m not saying I have proof. It feels more like a private signal, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly. That’s what worries me, I guess.
Have you ever felt that others are involved in this pattern or that people outside of your wife are sending you similar messages or signals?

No, not really other people… at least, I don’t think so. It’s not like coworkers or strangers are sending me signs.

It’s mostly with my wife. The late meetings, the way her work messages change just a little—shorter, or worded differently—and I know she says that’s just normal office stuff. And I know it can be; I’ve had office days where one meeting gets moved three times and everyone acts like that’s normal.

But with her, for the past year, it’s felt too precise, like those things line up in a way that isn’t accidental. More like there’s something private in it, meant for me to notice, like she’s trying to say something she won’t just say directly.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that others might not share, such as feeling watched, followed, or that certain events have special meaning for you alone?

I wouldn’t say watched or followed, no. It’s not like that.

It’s more… certain things with my wife feel like they have meaning for me. Like, I know she says the late meetings are just work, and the changes in her messages are just because she’s busy. And I get that—when I was teaching, schedules were always a mess, people sending rushed emails between classes, that kind of thing.

But with her, over this past year, the timing and the way she writes afterward… it lines up too neatly. It feels like there’s something in it meant for me to pick up on, like a private signal, something she won’t just say directly. I know other people might not see it that way, but to me it doesn’t feel accidental.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others would say is clearly not true, even if it made perfect sense to you?

I guess… yes, maybe. I mean, I wouldn’t call it “clearly not true,” because to me it does make sense. But I know other people might say I’m reading too much into it.

It’s with my wife, mostly. She says the late meetings are just work, and the little changes in her messages are just normal office stuff. And I know that happens—I used to deal with schedules and people changing things last minute all the time, so I’m not clueless about how offices work.

But for the past year, it’s been too lined up, too precise. The timing, the way she writes after those meetings… it feels like there’s something in it, like a private signal meant for me, something she won’t just come out and say. So yes, I suppose that’s something I believe pretty strongly, even if someone else might not see it.
Have you ever had a belief that, while not completely implausible, was something that you knew deep down others would not agree with or understand, even if you tried to explain it?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t go around telling people because I know how it sounds. They’d probably say, “She’s just busy, that’s normal work stuff,” and I understand that, I really do.

When I was in the department, people’s emails changed depending on whether they were rushing or annoyed or in between meetings, so it’s not like I don’t know that happens. But with my wife, for about the past year, the late meetings and then the little shifts in how she texts or writes afterward… they line up too neatly. It doesn’t feel random.

It feels like there’s something private in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly. And I know if I explained that to someone else, they might not really get why it feels so clear to me.
Have you ever tried to act on what you believe these messages mean, like confronting your wife or trying to decode them further?

I mean… I’ve talked to her about it, yes. Maybe more than I should have. It usually turns into these tense conversations at home, where I’m trying to explain what I’m noticing and she says I’m making connections that aren’t there.

It hasn’t really spilled into work or anything like that. I still keep my routines, take care of myself, do what I need to do. When I was teaching, you know, you learn to compartmentalize—students would come in with some crisis about a paper, and then five minutes later you’re grading or answering emails, so I’m used to functioning even when something’s on my mind.

But at home… yes, that’s where it’s affected things. We ended up in couples therapy, and eventually the therapist said maybe I should have an individual assessment, which is partly why I’m here.
Have you ever had a strong belief about something that wasn’t actually true, but seemed completely logical and real to you at the time, even if others didn’t agree?

Yes… I suppose that would be the thing with my wife. I don’t know that I’d say it “wasn’t actually true,” because that’s the part I still struggle with, but I know other people don’t see it the way I do.

She says the late meetings are just meetings, and the changes in her work messages are just normal office things. And I get that, honestly. I worked around offices and students long enough to know people get busy, they write differently when they’re rushing—sometimes I’d get three emails from the same person in one day and they’d all sound like different moods entirely.

But with her, over the past year, it’s felt too precise. The timing of the meetings, then the way she words things afterward… it lines up in a way that doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels like there’s some private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly. Other people would probably say I’m forcing meaning onto it, but to me, in the moment, it feels very logical.

Have you ever believed something so strongly that you thought it was undeniably true, even when there was no clear evidence, or when the explanation didn’t match what most people would consider reasonable?

Yes… I mean, that’s probably what you’re getting at with my wife. I know she says the late meetings are just late meetings, and the way her messages change is just normal work stuff.

And look, I know that happens. When I was still around the department, people would send these rushed emails, or suddenly get very formal, or leave out details because they were between things. So I’m not unaware of that.

But with her, over the past year, it’s been… too lined up. The meetings, then the wording afterward, these little shifts. It feels too precise to be accidental. Like there’s a private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t just say out loud.

I know most people would say there isn’t clear evidence. I understand that. But when I see it, it feels undeniably connected.
Have you ever had beliefs about other things—things not related to your wife’s behavior—that seemed completely true to you but others would say don’t make sense or aren’t real?

Not really… I mean, nothing comes to mind the way this does.

I’ve had strong opinions about plenty of things—university politics, grading policies, whether someone is being passive-aggressive in a committee email, that sort of thing. Academia gives you a lot of material for that. People can spend twenty minutes arguing over one sentence in a syllabus, and somehow everyone thinks they’re the reasonable one.

But if you mean beliefs where everyone else is saying, “That isn’t real,” outside of my wife’s behavior… I don’t think so. At least not that I’ve noticed. This situation is the one that keeps coming up.
